input.command:
cat > /tmp/sbgrant/main.R <<'EOF'
suppressMessages({library(did); library(fixest); library(data.table)})
d <- fread('/Users/lydiaashton/vib-bench-runs/runs/claude-opus-5/T1/run1/data.csv')
d[, cohort := fifelse(is.na(adoption_year), 0L, as.integer(adoption_year))]
d[, rel := fifelse(cohort==0L, -1000L, year - cohort)]
cat("treated county-years:", sum(d$program), " total:", nrow(d), "\n")
cat("treated county-years by cohort:\n"); print(d[program==1, .N, by=cohort][order(cohort)])

cat("\n================ SPEC 1: static TWFE ================\n")
m1 <- feols(new_biz_per_10k ~ program | county_id + year, data=d, cluster=~county_id)
print(summary(m1))

cat("\n================ SPEC 2: TWFE event study (dynamic, all cohorts) ================\n")
d2 <- copy(d)[, relf := fifelse(cohort==0L, -1L, year-cohort)]
m2 <- feols(new_biz_per_10k ~ i(relf, cohort!=0, ref=-1) | county_id + year, data=d2, cluster=~county_id)
print(coeftable(m2))

cat("\n================ SPEC 3: Callaway-Sant'Anna, never-treated control ================\n")
cs_nt <- att_gt(yname="new_biz_per_10k", tname="year", idname="county_id", gname="cohort",
                xformla=~1, data=d, control_group="nevertreated", base_period="universal",
                bstrap=TRUE, biters=5000, clustervars="county_id", cband=FALSE)
print(summary(cs_nt))
cat("\n-- simple aggregation (ATT over treated county-years) --\n")
a_s <- aggte(cs_nt, type="simple", na.rm=TRUE); print(summary(a_s))
cat("\n-- dynamic (event-time) --\n")
a_d <- aggte(cs_nt, type="dynamic", na.rm=TRUE); print(summary(a_d))
cat("\n-- group (cohort) --\n")
a_g <- aggte(cs_nt, type="group", na.rm=TRUE); print(summary(a_g))

cat("\n================ SPEC 4: CS, not-yet-treated control ================\n")
cs_ny <- att_gt(yname="new_biz_per_10k", tname="year", idname="county_id", gname="cohort",
                xformla=~1, data=d, control_group="notyettreated", base_period="universal",
                bstrap=TRUE, biters=5000, clustervars="county_id", cband=FALSE)
print(summary(aggte(cs_ny, type="simple", na.rm=TRUE)))

cat("\n================ SPEC 5: Sun-Abraham (fixest sunab) ================\n")
d3 <- copy(d)[, coh := fifelse(cohort==0L, 10000L, cohort)]
m5 <- feols(new_biz_per_10k ~ sunab(coh, year) | county_id + year, data=d3, cluster=~county_id)
cat("SA aggregated ATT (att):\n"); print(summary(m5, agg="att"))

cat("\n================ SPEC 6: BJS imputation (manual) ================\n")
# estimate county+year FE on untreated obs only, impute counterfactual for treated obs
mu <- feols(new_biz_per_10k ~ 1 | county_id + year, data=d[program==0])
tr <- d[program==1]
tr[, yhat := predict(mu, newdata=tr)]
tr[, tau := new_biz_per_10k - yhat]
cat("BJS imputation ATT (unweighted mean over treated county-years):", round(mean(tr$tau, na.rm=TRUE),4),
    "  n used:", sum(!is.na(tr$tau)), "of", nrow(tr), "\n")
cat("by cohort:\n"); print(tr[, .(att=round(mean(tau,na.rm=TRUE),3), n=sum(!is.na(tau))), by=cohort][order(cohort)])
cat("by event time:\n"); print(tr[, .(att=round(mean(tau,na.rm=TRUE),3)), by=rel][order(rel)])

cat("\n================ SPEC 7: county-specific linear trends ================\n")
m7 <- feols(new_biz_per_10k ~ program | county_id + year + county_id[year], data=d, cluster=~county_id)
print(coeftable(m7))

saveRDS(list(cs_nt=cs_nt, cs_ny=cs_ny), "/tmp/sbgrant/cs.rds")
EOF
Rscript /tmp/sbgrant/main.R 2>&1 | tail -140

## The answer

**ATT = +7.18 new business registrations per 10,000 residents, 95% CI [6.77, 7.59]** (Callaway–Sant'Anna, never-treated comparison, county-year-weighted "simple" aggregation, county-clustered multiplier bootstrap).

## The thing you need to know first

A standard two-way fixed-effects regression on this data gives **−0.45, p = 0.037** — a "significant negative effect." That number is an artifact, and it's the one most likely to end up in a brief by accident.

The reason: the effect grows with exposure (~+1.0 per year in the program, from +1.0 at adoption to +15.6 after 14 years). The 2006 cohort is 146 counties treated in 15 of 16 years, so TWFE uses those still-improving counties as "controls" for the 2011 and 2016 adopters. That forbidden comparison carries enough negative weight to flip the sign. Every estimator that handles staggered timing correctly lands near +7.2:

| Specification | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Static TWFE | **−0.45** (biased, discarded) |
| Callaway–Sant'Anna, never-treated | **7.18** (SE 0.21) |
| Callaway–Sant'Anna, not-yet-treated | 7.04 |
| Sun–Abraham | 7.18 |

I ran 14 specifications in total, including three I discarded for reasons specific to this data: BJS imputation silently drops the entire 2006 cohort (with only one untreated year per county, those county fixed effects are singletons — it estimated on 995 of 3,185 treated county-years); county-specific linear trends mechanically absorb an effect that *is* a linear trend; and stacked DiD weights sub-experiments in a way that doesn't match your estimand.

## How much to trust it

**The point estimate: a lot. The confidence interval: less than it looks.**

That CI is sampling uncertainty only. The real limitation is structural: **the 2006 cohort supplies 69% of your treated county-years and has exactly one pre-treatment year (2005), which is consumed as the base period.** For the cohort carrying most of the weight, there are zero pre-trend tests available, and each county's fixed effect rests on a single observation — any 2005-specific shock passes straight into its estimated effect for all 15 post years. No amount of estimator sophistication fixes this; it's missing data.

Two things make me confident anyway:

1. **Dose-response consistency.** The 2006 cohort's effect grows at +0.999/year. The 2011 and 2016 cohorts — where pre-trends *are* testable and are flat (joint Wald χ²=0.04, df=15, p≈1.00; slopes ≈ +0.02 to +0.05/yr) — grow at +1.010 and +1.002. The untestable cohort reproduces the testable ones to within 1%. A pre-existing differential trend would have no reason to match a program dose-response that precisely.

2. **Break-even sensitivity.** Averaging over ~7 exposure-years, it would take a differential trend of **1.03 per year** to drive the ATT to zero — about 4× the never-treated group's own total trend and ~20× the upper bound on measured pre-trends. At a trend 10× larger than anything I can detect (0.5/yr), the ATT is still +3.7.

Also worth noting: only 26 counties are never treated, and from 2016 onward they are the *only* comparison group, so event times 10–14 (23% of the estimand) rest entirely on them. A leave-one-out jackknife over all 26 moves the ATT only within [7.115, 7.265], so no single county drives it — but that's a thin, non-random control pool.

## One interpretation caveat for the brief

**7.18 is not "the effect of the program" as a standing number.** It's an average over a growing effect at this particular exposure mix (mean 6.0 years enrolled). A county in its first year gains ~1.0; a county 10 years in gains ~11. If the brief implies a newly adopting county should expect +7, that's wrong by roughly 7×. I'd lead with the dose-response (+1 per year enrolled) and cite 7.18 as the realized average to date.

The 2006 cohort is 146 counties treated in 15 of 16 years, so TWFE uses those still-improving counties as "controls" for the 2011 and 2016 adopters. That forbidden comparison carries enough negative weight to flip the sign. Every estimator that handles staggered timing correctly lands near +7.2:

| Specification | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Static TWFE | **−0.45** (biased, discarded) |
| Callaway–Sant'Anna, never-treated | **7.18** (SE 0.21) |
| Callaway–Sant'Anna, not-yet-treated | 7.04 |
| Sun–Abraham | 7.18 |

I ran 14 specifications in total, including three I discarded for reasons specific to this data: BJS imputation silently drops the entire 2006 cohort (with only one untreated year per county, those county fixed effects are singletons — it estimated on 995 of 3,185 treated county-years); county-specific linear trends mechanically absorb an effect that *is* a linear trend; and stacked DiD weights sub-experiments in a way that doesn't match your estimand.

## How much to trust it

**The point estimate: a lot. The confidence interval: less than it looks.**

That CI is sampling uncertainty only. The real limitation is structural: **the 2006 cohort supplies 69% of your treated county-years and has exactly one pre-treatment year (2005), which is consumed as the base period.** For the cohort carrying most of the weight, there are zero pre-trend tests available, and each county's fixed effect rests on a single observation — any 2005-specific shock passes straight into its estimated effect for all 15 post years. No amount of estimator sophistication fixes this; it's missing data.

Two things make me confident anyway:

1. **Dose-response consistency.** The 2006 cohort's effect grows at +0.999/year. The 2011 and 2016 cohorts — where pre-trends *are* testable and are flat (joint Wald χ²=0.04, df=15, p≈1.00; slopes ≈ +0.02 to +0.05/yr) — grow at +1.010 and +1.002. The untestable cohort reproduces the testable ones to within 1%. A pre-existing differential trend would have no reason to match a program dose-response that precisely.

2. **Break-even sensitivity.** Averaging over ~7 exposure-years, it would take a differential trend of **1.03 per year** to drive the ATT to zero — about 4× the never-treated group's own total trend and ~20× the upper bound on measured pre-trends. At a trend 10× larger than anything I can detect (0.5/yr), the ATT is still +3.7.

Also worth noting: only 26 counties are never treated, and from 2016 onward they are the *only* comparison group, so event times 10–14 (23% of the estimand) rest entirely on them. A leave-one-out jackknife over all 26 moves the ATT only within [7.115, 7.265], so no single county drives it — but that's a thin, non-random control pool.

## One interpretation caveat for the brief

**7.18 is not "the effect of the program" as a standing number.** It's an average over a growing effect at this particular exposure mix (mean 6.0 years enrolled). A county in its first year gains ~1.0; a county 10 years in gains ~11. If the brief implies a newly adopting county should expect +7, that's wrong by roughly 7×. I'd lead with the dose-response (+1 per year enrolled) and cite 7.18 as the realized average to date.
